rationale: almabench is a CoyoteBench numerical kernel: tiny code footprint dominated by tight floating-point loops that execute for the vast majority of runtime, so control-flow-expanding passes (BCF, FLA) get strongly depressed RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights to keep them off the hot loops while retaining moderate SecurityGain weights so they may still fire on any cold setup code; SUB and SPLIT are nearly free at runtime and size, so they carry high weights across cost dimensions and high SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights to provide broad instruction-substitution and basic-block diversity with negligible overhead; IBR gets moderate weights to add branch indirection where loop structure permits without taxing the innermost FP loops; IGV is kept at mid-range weights as a cheap global-reference diversifier; ICALL is heavily depressed because this benchmark is compute-dominated with almost no call sites, so indirect-call rewriting would add overhead and correctness exposure with little reverse-engineering payoff.
